title: Dependency declared with a bare wildcard range
what: a dependency specifier of `*`, which accepts every version the registry has ever published
impact: Any release, including one published after this manifest was reviewed, satisfies the declaration, so the install is not reproducible and a compromised publish is taken automatically.
remediation: Pin the dependency to an exact version or to the narrowest range the project tests.
limitation: It matches a dependency specifier of `*`, which accepts every version the registry has ever published in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A manifest that documents the wildcard in a README or a fixture is not reported.

title: Dependency declared with an empty version specifier
what: an empty dependency specifier, which npm reads as `*`
impact: An empty specifier accepts any version, so the lockfile decides what runs and a fresh install can resolve a version nobody reviewed.
remediation: Write an explicit version or range; an empty string is never a deliberate pin.
limitation: It matches an empty dependency specifier, which npm reads as `*` in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A generated manifest that writes an empty string for an optional peer is not reported when the dependency is absent.

title: Dependency pinned to the latest dist-tag
what: a dependency pinned to the `latest` dist-tag instead of a version
impact: The tag moves whenever the publisher releases, so a build resolves a different version than the one that was reviewed and tested.
remediation: Replace the dist-tag with the concrete version the project tested.
limitation: It matches a dependency pinned to the `latest` dist-tag instead of a version in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A tooling script that documents `latest` in prose is not reported.

title: Dependency declared with an x-range major
what: an `N.x` major range, which accepts every minor and patch release of that major
impact: Any release in the major line satisfies the declaration, so a breaking or compromised minor reaches the build without a manifest change.
remediation: Declare the minor range the project tests, or pin an exact version with the lockfile committed.
limitation: It matches an `N.x` major range, which accepts every minor and patch release of that major in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A manifest that pins a caret range on the same major is not reported by this rule.

title: Dependency declared with a wildcard minor
what: an `N.*` minor wildcard, which accepts every minor and patch release of that major
impact: The wildcard hides which release the build actually used, and a newly published minor is picked up on the next install without review.
remediation: Declare the concrete minor version and let the lockfile pin the patch.
limitation: It matches an `N.*` minor wildcard, which accepts every minor and patch release of that major in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A caret range on the same major is a different declaration and is not reported.

title: Dependency fetched over the unauthenticated git protocol
what: a dependency URL that uses the `git://` protocol
impact: The git protocol carries no transport authentication for the fetched objects, so a network attacker can substitute the tree the install compiles.
remediation: Fetch over `git+https://` with a commit sha, or publish the package to the registry.
limitation: It matches a dependency URL that uses the `git://` protocol in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A local mirror configured for `git://` inside a hardened build network is a policy exception, not a detection difference.

title: Dependency installed from a git checkout
what: a dependency installed from a git remote rather than the registry
impact: The recorded version is a commit the registry never vetted, the tarball has no registry integrity value, and the repository can be rewritten after review.
remediation: Prefer a published version with registry integrity, or pin the commit sha and record the resolved hash.
limitation: It matches a dependency installed from a git remote rather than the registry in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A git dependency whose commit is pinned and whose build verifies the checkout is still reported: the rule names the source kind, not its safety.

title: Dependency installed over SSH from a git remote
what: a dependency installed from a git remote over SSH
impact: The install trusts whatever host key and account the build machine has, so the code that runs is decided outside the registry and outside the lockfile hash.
remediation: Publish the artifact to a private registry with integrity, or pin the commit and verify the checkout digest.
limitation: It matches a dependency installed from a git remote over SSH in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A private registry that itself speaks SSH internally is out of scope: the rule looks at the manifest specifier only.

title: Dependency declared with the GitHub shorthand
what: the `github:` dependency shorthand, which resolves a repository default branch
impact: The shorthand follows whatever branch the repository publishes, so the installed tree can change without any manifest edit.
remediation: Depend on a published version, or pin `github:owner/repo#<commit-sha>` and record the resolved commit.
limitation: It matches the `github:` dependency shorthand, which resolves a repository default branch in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A shorthand naming a commit sha is still reported as a non-registry source; the rule reports the source kind.

title: Dependency declared with the GitLab shorthand
what: the `gitlab:` dependency shorthand
impact: The shorthand resolves from a forge the registry never vetted and follows a moving reference, so the packaged bytes are not the reviewed bytes.
remediation: Publish the artifact with a version and integrity, or pin the shorthand to a commit sha.
limitation: It matches the `gitlab:` dependency shorthand in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A shorthand naming a commit is reported too; the rule names the resolver, not the pin quality.

title: Dependency declared with the Bitbucket shorthand
what: the `bitbucket:` dependency shorthand
impact: The install resolves a forge reference that the registry never attested, and the resolved commit can change while the manifest stays identical.
remediation: Use a registry version with integrity, or a shorthand pinned to a commit sha.
limitation: It matches the `bitbucket:` dependency shorthand in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A sibling shorthand for a different forge is not reported by this rule.

title: Dependency installed from an anonymous gist
what: a gist dependency, which resolves an anonymous paste rather than a package
impact: A gist has no publisher identity, no registry attestation and no integrity value, so the code that runs is whatever the paste holds when the install fetches it.
remediation: Move the code into a reviewed package, or vendor it with a recorded hash.
limitation: It matches a gist dependency, which resolves an anonymous paste rather than a package in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A gist that happens to be owned by the same organisation is still reported; the rule reports the resolver kind.

title: Dependency declared with a bare owner/repo shorthand
what: a bare `owner/repo` specifier, which npm expands to a GitHub install
impact: The specifier names a repository rather than a published artifact, so no registry integrity protects the tree that is compiled.
remediation: Install the published package, or write `github:owner/repo#<sha>` so the source is explicit and pinned.
limitation: It matches a bare `owner/repo` specifier, which npm expands to a GitHub install in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A scoped registry name such as `@acme/sdk` is a package name, not a shorthand, and is not reported.

title: Dependency installed from a plain tarball URL
what: a dependency URL that points at a tarball outside the configured registry
impact: The tarball is fetched without a registry signature or provenance attestation, and the URL can serve different bytes on every install.
remediation: Publish the artifact to the registry and depend on the version, so the lockfile records an integrity hash.
limitation: It matches a dependency URL that points at a tarball outside the configured registry in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A registry tarball URL written by a mirror configuration is a separate finding; this rule reports deployment-owned URLs.

title: Dependency fetched over cleartext HTTP
what: a dependency URL that uses cleartext `http://`
impact: Cleartext transport lets a network attacker replace the artifact in flight, and the substitution is invisible after the install succeeds.
remediation: Serve the artifact over HTTPS, or install from the registry.
limitation: It matches a dependency URL that uses cleartext `http://` in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A local `http://127.0.0.1` mirror inside an isolated build is reported as well; record it as an accepted exception if that is the policy.

title: Dependency resolved from a local path
what: a `file:` dependency that points at a path on the build machine
impact: The installed code is whatever sits at that path at build time, so the artifact is not reproducible from the manifest and a local edit ships without review.
remediation: Publish the package to a private registry, or use a workspace with a lockfile entry that records the resolved content.
limitation: It matches a `file:` dependency that points at a path on the build machine in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A monorepo workspace that intentionally links its own packages is still reported; treat it as an accepted policy exception.

title: Dependency linked as a symlink to a local directory
what: a `link:` dependency, which installs a symlink instead of a package
impact: Nothing is copied into the artifact, so the dependency resolves to a directory that may not exist or may differ on any other machine.
remediation: Depend on a published version, and keep local linking to development-only overrides that never ship.
limitation: It matches a `link:` dependency, which installs a symlink instead of a package in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: Development overrides outside the shipped manifest are not reported by this rule.

title: Dependency resolved through the portal protocol
what: a `portal:` dependency, a Yarn protocol that resolves a live directory
impact: The consumer reads the directory at run time, so the package contents are not frozen by the install and can change between builds.
remediation: Publish the package and depend on a version that the lockfile pins.
limitation: It matches a `portal:` dependency, a Yarn protocol that resolves a live directory in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: The sibling `link:` protocol is a different resolver and is not reported here.

title: Dependency resolved through the workspace protocol
what: a `workspace:` specifier, which resolves a sibling workspace instead of a registry version
impact: The published artifact can keep a workspace protocol that a consumer cannot resolve, or silently substitute a sibling package for the dependency the manifest names.
remediation: Use the workspace protocol only in private packages, and rewrite it to a registry version before publishing.
limitation: It matches a `workspace:` specifier, which resolves a sibling workspace instead of a registry version in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A private root manifest that is never published is still reported; the rule reads the manifest, not the publish state.

title: Dependency installed under an alias of another package
what: an `npm:` alias that installs a differently named package under this dependency name
impact: Every reader of the manifest sees one name while a different package runs, which defeats name-based review and allow-lists.
remediation: Depend on the package under its real name, and record any rename in the review.
limitation: It matches an `npm:` alias that installs a differently named package under this dependency name in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: An alias used by a tooling shim with a documented owner is an accepted exception.

title: Git dependency pinned through a semver fragment
what: a git dependency whose fragment asks npm to resolve a semver range instead of committing to one tree
impact: The install resolves the range against the remote's tags at fetch time, so the compiled tree can move without a manifest change and without a lockfile review.
remediation: Pin the fragment to a full commit sha and record the resolved commit in review.
limitation: It matches a git dependency whose fragment asks npm to resolve a semver range instead of committing to one tree in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A fragment naming a full commit sha is a different declaration and is not reported.

title: Git dependency pinned to a short commit fragment
what: a git dependency pinned to a commit fragment rather than a registry version
impact: The commit is immutable but outside the registry, so no registry attestation, signature or advisory range covers the code that runs.
remediation: Prefer a published version; when a commit is unavoidable, review the diff at that sha and record why the registry cannot be used.
limitation: It matches a git dependency pinned to a commit fragment rather than a registry version in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A fragment naming a branch or tag is reported by the branch rule, not this one.

title: Dependency declared with an open lower bound
what: a `>=` specifier with no upper bound
impact: Every future major release satisfies the declaration, so an incompatible or compromised release is installed without a manifest change.
remediation: Add an upper bound the project tests, or pin an exact version.
limitation: It matches a `>=` specifier with no upper bound in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A `>=` paired with `<` in the same specifier has a bound and is not reported.

title: Dependency declared with a strict open bound
what: a `>` specifier that excludes the named version and every version above it
impact: The declaration accepts an unbounded set of future releases and cannot be satisfied by the version the manifest names, so review and install disagree.
remediation: State the exact version or a closed range.
limitation: It matches a `>` specifier that excludes the named version and every version above it in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A `>` combined with an upper bound is a closed range and is not reported.

title: Dependency declared with a caret on a zero-zero version
what: a caret range on a `0.0.x` version, which npm treats as an exact patch lock
impact: The declaration looks like a range but admits only one patch, so a security fix in the next patch never installs while the manifest appears permissive.
remediation: Write the exact version the project tests, or move to a maintained major line.
limitation: It matches a caret range on a `0.0.x` version, which npm treats as an exact patch lock in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A caret on `0.x.y` where the minor is non-zero has different semantics and is not reported here.

title: Dependency declared with a caret inside a zero major line
what: a caret range inside a `0.x` line, where npm only allows patch-level movement
impact: Consumers expecting minor updates never receive them, so fixes that ship in the next minor stay out of the build while the range reads as a normal caret.
remediation: State the minor version explicitly and review each upgrade.
limitation: It matches a caret range inside a `0.x` line, where npm only allows patch-level movement in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A caret on a stable major (`^1.x`) follows different rules and is not reported.

title: Dependency declared with a hyphen range
what: a hyphen range that spans several minor or major releases
impact: The range accepts every release between the two ends, including ones published after review, so an upgrade happens silently on the next install.
remediation: Pin the version under test, or narrow the range to one tested line.
limitation: It matches a hyphen range that spans several minor or major releases in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A hyphen range inside a single patch line is still a range and is reported; narrow it to an exact version.

title: Dependency declared with an either-or range
what: an `||` range that lets two different major lines satisfy one declaration
impact: The installing machine, not the manifest, decides which line runs, so two builds of the same commit can compile different code.
remediation: Choose one line, pin it, and record the migration to the other.
limitation: It matches an `||` range that lets two different major lines satisfy one declaration in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A generator that writes an either-or range for a compatibility window is still reported; record it as an accepted exception.

title: Dependency pinned to a prerelease build
what: an exact pin to a prerelease build
impact: Prerelease builds carry no stability promise and are frequently outside advisory ranges, so a known defect can ship while the pin looks deliberate and exact.
remediation: Pin the first stable release once it exists, and record the review that approved a prerelease.
limitation: It matches an exact pin to a prerelease build in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A range that merely permits a prerelease is a different declaration and is not reported here.

title: Dependency pinned with build metadata
what: a version carrying `+build` metadata
impact: Build metadata is ignored by precedence but not by every resolver, so two tools can disagree about which artifact the pin names.
remediation: Pin the plain semantic version and record the build identity elsewhere.
limitation: It matches a version carrying `+build` metadata in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A version whose metadata mirrors a registry-published artifact is still reported; the rule reads the declaration.

title: Dependency pinned to a placeholder zero version
what: a pin to `0.0.0`, the placeholder version package managers publish before a real release
impact: The placeholder usually means an unpublished or local-only artifact, so the dependency resolves differently on any machine without the same local state.
remediation: Publish a real version and pin it, or vendor the code with a recorded hash.
limitation: It matches a pin to `0.0.0`, the placeholder version package managers publish before a real release in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A deliberately published `0.0.0` bootstrap artifact is still reported; record the exception.

title: Dependency declared with a v-prefixed version
what: a version written with a `v` prefix, which is a tag name rather than a semantic version
impact: npm resolves the text as a dist-tag or rejects it, so the install depends on what the registry happens to have tagged rather than on the version the review saw.
remediation: Write the semantic version without the prefix.
limitation: It matches a version written with a `v` prefix, which is a tag name rather than a semantic version in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A `v` inside a git URL fragment is part of that URL and is not reported here.

title: Dependency declared with a four-part version
what: a four-part version, which is not a semantic version
impact: Resolvers disagree about how the fourth component orders, so the version that installs can differ between npm, a mirror and a CI cache.
remediation: Use a semantic three-part version published to the registry.
limitation: It matches a four-part version, which is not a semantic version in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A four-part version inside a build identifier string is not a specifier and is not reported.

title: Dependency declared with a date-shaped version
what: a date-shaped version, which carries no compatibility signal
impact: A calendar version cannot tell the resolver whether two releases are compatible, so a rollback or upgrade cannot be reasoned about from the manifest.
remediation: Depend on a semantic version and record the release date in the changelog.
limitation: It matches a date-shaped version, which carries no compatibility signal in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A three-part calendar version such as `2025.1.4` is reported too; the shape is the finding.

title: Dependency declared with an implausibly large major
what: a major version far larger than any the project has published
impact: Dependency-confusion and typosquat campaigns publish inflated versions so a permissive range resolves to them; the pin is what makes that possible.
remediation: Pin the version that the project actually tested against its registry.
limitation: It matches a major version far larger than any the project has published in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A project that legitimately uses date-based majors is still reported; record the exception.

title: Dependency declared only by exclusions
what: a specifier that names only versions to exclude
impact: An exclusion-only declaration accepts every other release, including every future one, so the dependency is effectively unbounded.
remediation: Add an upper bound or pin the exact version under test.
limitation: It matches a specifier that names only versions to exclude in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: An exclusion written inside a closed range is bounded and is not reported.

title: Dependency declared with RubyGems range syntax
what: a `~>` range, which is RubyGems syntax rather than npm syntax
impact: npm resolves the text as an unknown comparator or a tag, so the install either fails or follows a reference nobody reviewed.
remediation: Write the npm range the project means (`~4.2.0` or an exact version).
limitation: It matches a `~>` range, which is RubyGems syntax rather than npm syntax in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A `~>` inside a Gemfile is a different artifact and is handled by the rubygems rules.

title: Git dependency that follows a branch name
what: a git dependency whose fragment names a branch instead of a commit
impact: The branch moves, so every install can compile a different tree while the manifest and the review record stay identical.
remediation: Pin the fragment to a commit sha and update it deliberately.
limitation: It matches a git dependency whose fragment names a branch instead of a commit in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A fragment naming a tag is also mutable and is reported by the tag rule, not this one.

title: Git dependency that follows a tag name
what: a git dependency fragment that names a tag rather than a commit
impact: A tag can be force-moved by whoever controls the remote, so the installed tree is mutable even though the manifest looks pinned.
remediation: Pin the commit sha the tag currently points at.
limitation: It matches a git dependency fragment that names a tag rather than a commit in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A branch fragment is a different mutable reference and is reported separately.

title: Dependency declared as a direct registry URL
what: a dependency written as a registry URL rather than a version
impact: The URL bypasses the integrity value the lockfile would record and can point at a mirror that serves different content than the public registry.
remediation: Depend on the package name and a version so the lockfile records the integrity hash.
limitation: It matches a dependency written as a registry URL rather than a version in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A tarball URL is reported by the tarball rule; this rule covers registry-style paths.

title: Dependency fetched from a source archive URL
what: a dependency pointing at a forge source archive instead of a package
impact: The archive is generated on demand from a branch or tag, so the bytes are not the published artifact and carry no registry integrity value.
remediation: Publish a package and depend on its version.
limitation: It matches a dependency pointing at a forge source archive instead of a package in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A source archive with a commit sha is immutable but still outside the registry; it is reported as the same source kind.

title: Dependency declared with a multi-segment wildcard
what: a multi-segment wildcard that accepts every version of every major
impact: The declaration is unbounded in every segment, so the install follows whatever the registry publishes next, including a compromised release.
remediation: Pin the tested version.
limitation: It matches a multi-segment wildcard that accepts every version of every major in the parsed package.json; it cannot tell whether the package is installed, whether any published version is affected by an advisory, or whether the dependency reaches production code.
fp: A single-segment wildcard is a different declaration and is reported by the bare-wildcard rule.
